dominant_mechanisms: capture-to-organize ratio determines whether the system helps or delays action

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Throughput is dominated by capture speed, rescheduling speed, and glanceability of the current list.

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Extra workflow layers matter more here because the core job is often just remember, choose, and complete.

dominant_mechanisms: the category is governed by triage speed under message volume rather than deep configuration breadth

trust depends on whether users can reliably tell what has been handled, deferred, or delegated
tools survive when they keep message state legible while reducing scan cost and routing friction

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Safety means confidence that archive, snooze, follow-up, and send actions leave the mailbox in an understandable state.

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Coordination appears as clear waiting states, delegation visibility, and thread context for collaborative email work.

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Extra workflow concepts hurt more here because email is already an overloaded coordination channel.

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Activation friction is the cost of rules, training, or migration before the inbox feels faster.

constraint_interactions.mechanism_effect: Safety depends on whether changing status, scope, or assignees feels predictable and socially legible.

dominant_mechanisms: the category turns on how much structure the tool enforces versus how much state the user must manage manually
